comments.content: The logic `if (*hi || *f)` resets `lang_length` and continues the loop when either hearing_impaired OR forced is detected. This means if a filename has both tags (e.g., 'foo.en.forced.hi.srt'), only the first one encountered will be processed, and the second will be ignored because the loop continues with `lang_length = 0`. The tags should be processed independently without skipping the rest of the filename parsing.

The variable `checked_tag` is now used for both 'hi/sdh/cc' and 'forced' suffixes, but the name suggests it only checks one tag. Consider renaming to `checked_suffix` or similar for clarity. Also, the logic only allows one suffix to be checked per delimiter position due to `checked_tag = true` - if a filename has multiple suffixes separated by delimiters (e.g., 'foo.en.forced.hi.srt'), only the first will be recognized.
